definitions.meaning: a headlong rush or undue haste is one sense of the word
rain, snow and hail all count as water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone hurries out to watch the rain come down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hasty rash action and moisture falling from clouds, so both halves of the clue fit.

parts.note: casually turning up somewhere is one reading; being furled into a cylinder shape, like a tube, is the other

explanation.surface: A commuter gets to work on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground, but the clue is about something being rolled into a cylinder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means turning up casually, and the question mark admits the second, literal picture of a rug wound into a tube.

indicators.note: containing says the word for tin holds the river inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A can of food holds a bird caught from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a kind of domestic fowl.

definitions.meaning: a demonstration that something is true, as in evidence
the standard measure of alcohol content in spirits like whisky

explanation.surface: Someone shows how strong their resolve is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' reads as courage, but it is alcohol: a spirit's strength is measured in degrees on this scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means conclusive evidence, and also the measure of alcoholic strength in distilled drink.

definitions.meaning: in engineering, the allowable variation from a specified measurement

explanation.surface: Accepting that a little deviation will be allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means patient endurance, and in engineering the allowed margin of error in a dimension.

clue.text: Siren may lure soldier on board ship

parts.note: to lure is to tempt
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps, so a soldier
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A siren might entice a soldier aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board ship' looks like a container, but the soldier simply sits before the ship in a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren, from the Greek myth of singers luring sailors to wreck, is a seductive woman.

clue.text: A poor actor gets round about in America

indicators.note: about says the words before it are turned around

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, bad performer
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: An American ham actor goes on a tour of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns the whole run AHAMO backwards; 'in America' defines by location, as Omaha is a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, so a place found in the United States.

definitions.meaning: a settlement or adjustment made to suit circumstances
rooms in which to live or lodge

explanation.surface: Adjusting oneself to a new home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an adjustment or compromise, and also lodgings or housing.

clue.text: Patronising Tory on the way down

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
going down means descending

explanation.surface: A snooty Conservative politician whose career is in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Being patronising means treating others as inferior, a close synonym of talking down to them.

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the abbreviation for company
around tells us to move the letters of plays about

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe's productions include a dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' poses as theatre productions but is only fodder: 'around' turns it into ALYPS, set in the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The calypso is a West Indian style of song and dance from Trinidad.

clue.text: Complaint that chimney's black from that time

parts.note: a lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ago means back in time from now

explanation.surface: Someone moans that the chimney has been sooty for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is a Scottish word for chimney, unfamiliar to many solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment, and lumbago is pain in the lower back.

clue.text: Stars seen going round foreign capital

indicators.note: going round says one word wraps around the other

parts.note: something that is going, like a show running, is on
Rio de Janeiro was once Brazil's capital

explanation.surface: Stars are spotted touring an overseas capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960, when it moved to Brasilia.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a constellation, a named group of stars depicting a hunter.

definitions.meaning: obtained straight from the source, without intermediaries
the hand that comes first in a game of cards, or the player who comes first

explanation.surface: Instruct whoever won the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means direct or personal experience, and read as two words names the top-ranked player or hand.

indicators.note: sounds like says a word is spoken and another spelling heard

parts.note: a mite is a tiny creature or a very small amount

explanation.surface: A remark that tiny power is audible.
explanation.definitionFit: Might means strength or force, a straightforward synonym of power.

definitions.meaning: an old word for a seaman, from which the short word tar comes

explanation.surface: An old seaman's oilskin covering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in the first definition is read as 'is', joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old name for a sailor and also a waterproof canvas sheet.

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
verses are lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A protest against poetry as a means of discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk, so the verb form converses matches talks.

clue.text: Chartered accountant no good without provocation

parts.note: useless means no good

explanation.surface: An accountant is hopeless when unprovoked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without cause or reason has no provocation behind it.

clue.text: Dissipated bear smell is of no importance

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for trivial matters; here read as adjectival

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters are dispersed

explanation.surface: A dissolute bear's odour hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissipated' looks like an adjective for the bear, but rearranges BEAR SMELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for something trivial, from weak beer drunk in former times.

indicators.note: on places the river after the word for leave

parts.note: to leave is to depart
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Leaving a flower behind when you go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword joke for a river (it flows); the Ure runs through Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A going, as a noun, is a leaving, which is a departure.

definitions.meaning: a pointed wooden stick driven into the ground
a share or financial involvement in something

explanation.surface: A posting about an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a wooden post and also a share or vested interest in a venture.

clue.text: Meant, perhaps, to follow trial of will?

indicators.note: to follow puts the shuffled letters after the word for trial

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible alternative arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A remark on intended consequences after a court case about a will.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'will' is the legal document, not intention; 'perhaps' turns 'Meant' into AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of property after death.

indicators.note: placed outside says the word for placed wraps around the man

parts.note: to place something is to set it
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A leaflet left out by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet can be a single printed page or broadsheet, like a pamphlet.

parts.note: the Model T Ford car

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A stiff fashion model was spotted leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a fashion model, but it is the Ford Model T; 'off' rearranges SEEN to ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means stretched tight or stiff, a close synonym of rigid.

definitions.meaning: marked with lines, like lined paper

explanation.surface: A manager's paperwork set out neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means governed, and also marked with straight lines, as on writing paper.

clue.text: Old letters returned by Chinese nurse

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ancient writing is sent back by a nurse from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reads backwards the run SENUR that bridges 'Chinese nurse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are the characters of the ancient Germanic alphabets, so old letters.

clue.text: Is incumbent on someone to have done with falsehood

parts.note: something done with is over
a lie is a falsehood

explanation.surface: Someone has a duty to stop telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incumbent' reads as obligatory, but here means literally lying on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlie is to lie over or upon something, the literal sense of incumbent.

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name
keen means eager

explanation.surface: A young woman is keen to get some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing in China.

clue.text: Makes up garlands with flower when convenient

parts.note: to atone is to make amends or make up for something
leis are Hawaiian flower garlands
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Someone apologises with garlands of flowers whenever it suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' again means a river, the Yorkshire Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning at a time that suits oneself, without hurry.
